### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)

- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# i3-style

Make your i3 config a little more stylish.

About

i3-style applies a theme to your i3 config file to change the colorscheme of window decorations and the different parts of i3bar. It is designed especially for people who frequently change colorschemes.

- Easy to try out new themes.
- Themes are easy to read, modify, and share.
- Modifies your theme in place; templates are not required.

Usage

Call the tool with the name of the theme (or a path to a theme file) and the output location. The tool will apply the theme to your i3 configuration.

Example:

    i3-style solarized -o ~/.config/i3/config --reload

Or apply a theme file directly:

    i3-style ~/.config/i3/solarized.yaml -o ~/.config/i3/config

Send us themes!

If you have a colorscheme you'd like to share, you can convert an existing i3 config to a theme file:

    i3-style --to-theme ~/.config/i3/config -o my-theme.yaml

Please consider contributing new themes.

# i3 config file (v4)
#
# Please see http://i3wm.org/docs/userguide.html for a complete reference!
#
# This config file uses keycodes (bindsym) and was written for the QWERTY
# layout.
#
# To get a config file with the same key positions, but for your current
# layout, use the i3-config-wizard
#

# Font for window titles. Will also be used by the bar unless a different font
# is used in the bar {} block below. ISO 10646 = Unicode
font -misc-fixed-medium-r-normal--13-120-75-75-C-70-iso10646-1
# The font above is very space-efficient, that is, it looks good, sharp and
# clear in small sizes. However, if you need a lot of unicode glyphs or
# right-to-left text rendering, you should instead use pango for rendering and
# chose a FreeType font, such as:
# font pango:DejaVu Sans Mono 10

# use Mouse+Mod1 to drag floating windows to their wanted position
floating_modifier Mod1

# start a terminal
bindsym Mod1+Return exec i3-sensible-terminal

# kill focused window
bindsym Mod1+Shift+q kill

# start dmenu (a program launcher)
bindsym Mod1+d exec dmenu_run
# There also is the (new) i3-dmenu-desktop which only displays applications
# shipping a .desktop file. It is a wrapper around dmenu, so you need that
# installed.
# bindsym Mod1+d exec --no-startup-id i3-dmenu-desktop

# change focus
bindsym Mod1+j focus left
bindsym Mod1+k focus down
bindsym Mod1+l focus up
bindsym Mod1+semicolon focus right

# alternatively, you can use the cursor keys:
bindsym Mod1+Left focus left
bindsym Mod1+Down focus down
bindsym Mod1+Up focus up
bindsym Mod1+Right focus right

# move focused window
bindsym Mod1+Shift+j move left
bindsym Mod1+Shift+k move down
bindsym Mod1+Shift+l move up
bindsym Mod1+Shift+semicolon move right

# alternatively, you can use the cursor keys:
bindsym Mod1+Shift+Left move left
bindsym Mod1+Shift+Down move down
bindsym Mod1+Shift+Up move up
bindsym Mod1+Shift+Right move right

# split in horizontal orientation
bindsym Mod1+h split h

# split in vertical orientation
bindsym Mod1+v split v

# enter fullscreen mode for the focused container
bindsym Mod1+f fullscreen

# change container layout (stacked, tabbed, toggle split)
bindsym Mod1+s layout stacking
bindsym Mod1+w layout tabbed
bindsym Mod1+e layout toggle split

# toggle tiling / floating
bindsym Mod1+Shift+space floating toggle

# change focus between tiling / floating windows
bindsym Mod1+space focus mode_toggle

# focus the parent container
bindsym Mod1+a focus parent

# focus the child container
#bindsym Mod1+d focus child

# move the currently focused window to the scratchpad
bindsym Mod1+Shift+minus move scratchpad

# Show the next scratchpad window or hide the focused scratchpad window.
# If there are multiple scratchpad windows, this command cycles through them.
bindsym Mod1+minus scratchpad show

# switch to workspace
bindsym Mod1+1 workspace 1
bindsym Mod1+2 workspace 2

import subprocess, os, re
env=dict(os.environ); env["PATH"]="/tmp/bin:"+env["PATH"]
base=open("full.yaml").read()
def run(text, args):
    if os.path.exists("lnout"): os.remove("lnout")
    open("t.yaml","w").write(text)
    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"]+args,capture_output=True,env=env)
    out = open("lnout").read() if os.path.exists("lnout") else None
    return (r.returncode, out, r.stdout.decode(), r.stderr.decode())
tests = {
 "no meta": base.replace("meta:\n  description: MY TEST THEME\n",""),
 "no colors": base.replace("colors:\n  red: \"#FF0000\"\n  green: \"#00FF00\"\n  blue: \"#0000FF\"\n  yellow: \"#FFFF00\"\n",""),
 "no bar_colors.active_workspace": base.replace("  active_workspace:\n    border: blue\n    background: yellow\n    text: red\n",""),
 "no window_colors.focused": re.sub(r"  focused:\n    border: red\n    background: green\n    text: blue\n    indicator: yellow\n","",base,count=1),
 "no separator in bar_colors": base.replace("  separator: green\n",""),
}
args=["t.yaml","-c","base","-o","lnout"]
for k,v in tests.items():
    rc,out,so,se=run(v,args)
    print("=== %s rc=%d"%(k,rc))
    print("  stderr=%r"%se)
    if out: print("  out first lines: %r"%out[:200].replace("\n","~"))

exec(open("/tmp/t/probe2.py").read())
import random
css_pairs=[l.split() for l in open("/tmp/t/css.txt").read().split("\n") if l.strip()]
extra=[("grey","#BEBEBE"),("gray","#808080"),("cyan","#00FFFF"),("magenta","#FF00FF"),("rebeccapurple","#663399"),
("lightgoldenrod","#FAE4B4"),("lightgoldenrodyellow","#FAE5D5"),("aqua","#00FFFF"),("fuchsia","#FF00FF"),

("lightgrey","#D3D3D3"),("dimgrey","#696969"),("slategrey","#708090"),("darkslategrey","#2F4F4F")]
DB=[(n,h) for n,h in css_pairs]+extra
def hx(s):
    s=s.lstrip('#')
    return tuple(int(s[i:i+2],16) for i in (0,2,4))
def dist(a,b): return sum((a[i]-b[i])**2 for i in range(3))
def nearest(x):
    vals=sorted([(dist(x,hx(h)),n,h) for n,h in DB])
    return vals[0], vals[1], vals[2]
def strip(n): return re.sub(r'-\d+$','',n)
def compare(qs, verbose=True):
    res=name_many(qs)
    bad=0
    for q in qs:
        got=res[q.lower()]
        best,second,third=nearest(hx(q))
        base=[strip(g) for g in got]
        if base[0]!=best[1]:
            bad+=1

    if verbose: print("mismatches %d of %d"%(bad,len(qs)))
    return bad
PY

import random
css_pairs=[l.split() for l in open("/tmp/t/css.txt").read().split("\n") if l.strip()]
def hx(s):
    s=s.lstrip('#'); return tuple(int(s[i:i+2],16) for i in (0,2,4))

# compute switch points along the gray ramp for a given DB list
def ramp_switches(db):
    res=[]
    prev=None
    for v in range(256):
        x=(v,v,v)
        best=sorted([(dist(x,hx(h)),n) for n,h in db])[0][1]
        if best!=prev: res.append((v,best)); prev=best
    return res
def ramp_observed(step=1, start=0):
    # observed via tool; do in batches, use names of each batch
    out=[]
    vs=list(range(start,256))
    for i in range(0,len(vs),SLOTS):
        batch=vs[i:i+SLOTS]
        hexes=["#%02x%02x%02x"%(v,v,v) for v in batch]
        rc,so,se=nametheme(slots_config(hexes))
        got=parse(so)
        # map value -> first name in collection order
        for v,h in zip(batch,hexes):
            n=[k for k,val in got.items() if val.lower()==h.lower()]
            out.append((v, n[0] if n else None))
    return out

import random
css_pairs=[l.split() for l in open("/tmp/t/css.txt").read().split("\n") if l.strip()]

random.seed(2024)
qs=["#%02X%02X%02X"%(random.randrange(256),random.randrange(256),random.randrange(256)) for _ in range(3000)]
bad=0; badnames={}
res=name_many(qs)

    got=res[q.lower()]
    best=sorted([(dist(hx(q),hx(h)),n) for n,h in db])[0][1]
    b=[strip(g) for g in got]
    if b[0]!=best:
        bad+=1; badnames.setdefault(b[0],0); badnames[b[0]]+=1
print("mismatches",bad,"of",len(qs))

PY"}

actions.command:
cd /tmp/t && python3 - <<'PY'
exec(open("/tmp/t/fit.py").read())
import random
css_pairs=[l.split() for l in open("/tmp/t/css.txt").read().split("\n") if l.strip()]
db=[(n,h) for n,h in css_pairs if n not in ("cyan","magenta","gray","lightgoldenrod","rebeccapurple","lightgoldenrodyellow","lightslategray")]
db+= [("aqua","#00FFFF"),("fuchsia","#FF00FF"),("grey","#808080"),("lightslategrey","#778899")]
random.seed(2024)
qs=["#%02X%02X%02X"%(random.randrange(256),random.randrange(256),random.randrange(256)) for _ in range(3000)]
bad=0; badnames={}
res=name_many(qs)
for q in qs:
    got=res[q.lower()]
    best=sorted([(dist(hx(q),hx(h)),n) for n,h in db])[0][1]
    b=[strip(g) for g in got]
    if b[0]!=best:
        bad+=1; badnames.setdefault(b[0],0); badnames[b[0]]+=1
print("mismatches",bad,"of",len(qs))
print(badnames)
PY

import itertools, math
A=[hx(h) for n,h in DB]

def minDB(x):

    for a,c in zip(A,C):
        d=c-2*(a[0]*x[0]+a[1]*x[1]+a[2]*x[2])
        v=s+d
        if best is None or v<best: best=v
    return best

    cons=[]
    for q in queries:
        x=hx(q); r=minDB(x)
        cons.append((x,r))
    # sort by radius ascending
    cons.sort(key=lambda t:t[1])
    x0,r0=cons[0]
    box=[]
    for i in range(3):
        lo=max(0, x0[i]-int(math.sqrt(r0))); hi=min(255, x0[i]+int(math.sqrt(r0)))
        box.append(range(lo,hi+1))
    sols=[]
    for a in itertools.product(*box):
        ok=True
        for x,r in cons:
            d=(a[0]-x[0])**2+(a[1]-x[1])**2+(a[2]-x[2])**2
            if d>r: ok=False; break
        if ok: sols.append(a)

import subprocess, re, os
ENV=dict(os.environ); ENV["PATH"]="/tmp/bin:"+ENV["PATH"]
def slots_config(colors):
    colors=list(colors)+["#FF00FF"]*(25-len(colors))
    def ws(k,i): return "    %s %s %s %s"%(k,colors[i],colors[i+1],colors[i+2])
    cfg=["bar {","  colors {",
         "    separator "+colors[0],
         "    background "+colors[1],
         "    statusline "+colors[2],
         ws("focused_workspace",3),
         ws("urgent_workspace",6),
         "  }","}"]
    idx=9
    for c in ["focused","focused_inactive","unfocused","urgent"]:
        cfg.append("client.%s %s %s %s %s"%(c,colors[idx],colors[idx+1],colors[idx+2],colors[idx+3])); idx+=4
    return "\n".join(cfg)+"\n"
def probe(hexes, exe="/workspace/executable"):
    """returns list of (name,suffixcount?) per hex, batched over 25 slots"""
    res=[]
    hexes=list(hexes)
    for i in range(0,len(hexes),25):
        batch=hexes[i:i+25]
        open("/tmp/t/p.cfg","w").write(slots_config(batch))
        r=subprocess.run([exe,"--to-theme","/tmp/t/p.cfg"],capture_output=True,env=ENV)
        out=r.stdout.decode()
        d={}
        incol=False
        for line in out.split("\n"):
            if line.startswith("colors:"): incol=True; continue
            if incol:
                m=re.match(r'^  (\S+): "(.*?)"$', line)
                if m: d.setdefault(m.group(2).upper(),[]).append(m.group(1))
                elif line.strip()=="" : break
        for h in batch:
            res.append((h.upper(), d.get(h.upper(),[])))
    return res
def strip(n): return re.sub(r'-\d+$','',n)
def base_names(hexes):
    return [ [strip(n) for n in ns] for h,ns in probe(hexes)]

import json

def ntc_d(a,b):
    rmean=(a[0]+b[0])/2.0
    R=(a[0]-b[0])**2; G=(a[1]-b[1])**2; B=(a[2]-b[2])**2
    return 2*R+4*G+3*B+rmean*R/256.0
def nearest(x, metric):
    return min([(metric(x,a),n) for n,a in CSSVAL.items()])

    w=nearest(x, ntc_d)[1]
    if w!=t.split('-')[0]: bad+=1
print("ntc mismatches",bad,"of",len(samples))
def euc(a,b): return sum((a[i]-b[i])**2 for i in range(3))
bad=0
for x,t in samples:
    w=nearest(x, euc)[1]
    if w!=t.split('-')[0]: bad+=1
print("euc mismatches",bad,"of",len(samples))

def fit_plane(pts):
    n=len(pts)
    cx=sum(p[0] for p in pts)/n; cy=sum(p[1] for p in pts)/n; cz=sum(p[2] for p in pts)/n
    # covariance matrix (3x3)
    M=[[0.0]*3 for _ in range(3)]
    for p in pts:
        d=[p[0]-cx,p[1]-cy,p[2]-cz]
        for i in range(3):
            for j in range(3):
                M[i][j]+=d[i]*d[j]
    # smallest eigenvector via power iteration on inverse (use characteristic polynomial / Jacobi)
    # simple: use Jacobi eigenvalue algorithm
    import math, copy
    A=[row[:] for row in M]
    for _ in range(100):
        # find largest off-diagonal
        p,q=0,1; mv=abs(A[0][1])
        for i in range(3):
            for j in range(i+1,3):
                if abs(A[i][j])>mv: mv=abs(A[i][j]); p,q=i,j
        if mv<1e-12: break
        theta=0.5*math.atan2(2*A[p][q], A[q][q]-A[p][p])
        c=math.cos(theta); s=math.sin(theta)
        for k in range(3):
            akp=A[k][p]; akq=A[k][q]
            A[k][p]=c*akp-s*akq; A[k][q]=s*akp+c*akq
        for k in range(3):
            Apk=A[p][k]; Aqk=A[q][k]
            A[p][k]=c*Apk-s*Aqk; A[q][k]=s*Apk+c*Aqk
    eigs=[A[i][i] for i in range(3)]
    # eigenvectors: recompute via rotation accumulation
    # simpler: use characteristic eq for smallest eigenvalue
    # solve (M - lam I) v = 0 with lam = min eig using cofactor method
    lam=min(eigs)
    B=[[M[i][j]-(lam if i==j else 0) for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)]
    # cross product of two rows
    def cross(u,v): return [u[1]*v[2]-u[2]*v[1], u[2]*v[0]-u[0]*v[2], u[0]*v[1]-u[1]*v[0]]
    v1=cross(B[0],B[1]); v2=cross(B[0],B[2]); v3=cross(B[1],B[2])
    vec=max([v1,v2,v3], key=lambda v: sum(x*x for x in v))
    nn=math.sqrt(sum(x*x for x in vec))
    if nn<1e-12: return None
    vec=[x/nn for x in vec]
    o=vec[0]*cx+vec[1]*cy+vec[2]*cz
    return vec,o

    n=len(pts)
    cx=sum(p[0] for p in pts)/n; cy=sum(p[1] for p in pts)/n; cz=sum(p[2] for p in pts)/n
    # covariance matrix (3x3)
    M=[[0.0]*3 for _ in range(3)]
    for p in pts:
        d=[p[0]-cx,p[1]-cy,p[2]-cz]
        for i in range(3):
            for j in range(3):
                M[i][j]+=d[i]*d[j]
    # smallest eigenvector via power iteration on inverse (use characteristic polynomial / Jacobi)
    # simple: use Jacobi eigenvalue algorithm
    import math, copy
    A=[row[:] for row in M]
    for _ in range(100):
        # find largest off-diagonal
        p,q=0,1; mv=abs(A[0][1])
        for i in range(3):
            for j in range(i+1,3):
                if abs(A[i][j])>mv: mv=abs(A[i][j]); p,q=i,j
        if mv<1e-12: break
        theta=0.5*math.atan2(2*A[p][q], A[q][q]-A[p][p])
        c=math.cos(theta); s=math.sin(theta)
        for k in range(3):
            akp=A[k][p]; akq=A[k][q]
            A[k][p]=c*akp-s*akq; A[k][q]=s*akp+c*akq
        for k in range(3):
            Apk=A[p][k]; Aqk=A[q][k]
            A[p][k]=c*Apk-s*Aqk; A[q][k]=s*Apk+c*Aqk
    eigs=[A[i][i] for i in range(3)]
    # eigenvectors: recompute via rotation accumulation
    # simpler: use characteristic eq for smallest eigenvalue
    # solve (M - lam I) v = 0 with lam = min eig using cofactor method
    lam=min(eigs)
    B=[[M[i][j]-(lam if i==j else 0) for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)]
    # cross product of two rows
    def cross(u,v): return [u[1]*v[2]-u[2]*v[1], u[2]*v[0]-u[0]*v[2], u[0]*v[1]-u[1]*v[0]]
    v1=cross(B[0],B[1]); v2=cross(B[0],B[2]); v3=cross(B[1],B[2])
    vec=max([v1,v2,v3], key=lambda v: sum(x*x for x in v))
    nn=math.sqrt(sum(x*x for x in vec))
    if nn<1e-12: return None
    vec=[x/nn for x in vec]
    o=vec[0]*cx+vec[1]*cy+vec[2]*cz
    return vec,o

import collections, itertools, math
pts=[(r,g,b) for r in range(105,161,2) for g in range(105,161,2) for b in range(105,161,2)]
hs=["#%02X%02X%02X"%p for p in pts]
ns=[n[0] if n else "?" for n in base_names(hs)]
cell=collections.defaultdict(list)
for p,n in zip(pts,ns): cell[n].append(p)
print({k:len(v) for k,v in cell.items()})
def solve(name, cellpts, othervals):
    cons=[(x, min(sum((x[i]-a[i])**2 for i in range(3)) for a in othervals)) for x in cellpts]
    x0=min(cons,key=lambda t:t[1])
    r0=x0[1]
    box=[]
    for i in range(3):
        lo=max(0,x0[0][i]-int(math.sqrt(r0))-1); hi=min(255,x0[0][i]+int(math.sqrt(r0))+1)
        box.append(range(lo,hi+1))
    sols=[]
    for a in itertools.product(*box):
        ok=True
        for x,r in cons:
            if sum((a[i]-x[i])**2 for i in range(3))>r: ok=False;break
        if ok: sols.append(a)
    return sols

cd /tmp/t && timeout 900 python3 - <<'PY'
exec(open("/tmp/t/plane.py").read())
import collections, itertools, math
pts=[(r,g,b) for r in range(105,161,2) for g in range(105,161,2) for b in range(105,161,2)]
hs=["#%02X%02X%02X"%p for p in pts]
ns=[n[0] if n else "?" for n in base_names(hs)]
cell=collections.defaultdict(list)
for p,n in zip(pts,ns): cell[n].append(p)
print({k:len(v) for k,v in cell.items()})
def solve(name, cellpts, othervals):
    cons=[(x, min(sum((x[i]-a[i])**2 for i in range(3)) for a in othervals)) for x in cellpts]
    x0=min(cons,key=lambda t:t[1])
    r0=x0[1]
    box=[]
    for i in range(3):
        lo=max(0,x0[0][i]-int(math.sqrt(r0))-1); hi=min(255,x0[0][i]+int(math.sqrt(r0))+1)
        box.append(range(lo,hi+1))
    sols=[]
    for a in itertools.product(*box):
        ok=True
        for x,r in cons:
            if sum((a[i]-x[i])**2 for i in range(3))>r: ok=False;break
        if ok: sols.append(a)
    return sols
OTHER=[(105,105,105),(112,128,144),(119,136,153),(169,169,169),(192,192,192),(211,211,211),(220,220,220),(188,143,143),(95,158,160),(105,105,105)]
sols=solve('gray', cell['gray'], OTHER)
print("gray feasible:",len(sols), sols[:30])
sols=solve('grey', cell['grey'], OTHER)
print("grey feasible:",len(sols), sols[:30])
PY

data=[(tuple(x),t) for x,t in json.load(open("/tmp/t/big.json"))]

def dd(a,x): return sum((a[i]-x[i])**2 for i in range(3))
def solve_entry(name, othervals):
    inn=[x for x,t in data if t==name]
    if not inn: return []
    cons=[(x, min(dd(a,x) for a in othervals)) for x in inn]
    x0=min(inn,key=lambda x: min(dd(a,x) for a in othervals))
    r0=min(dd(a,x0) for a in othervals)
    box=[]
    for i in range(3):
        lo=max(0,x0[i]-int(math.sqrt(r0))-1); hi=min(255,x0[i]+int(math.sqrt(r0))+1)
        box.append(range(lo,hi+1))
    sols=[]
    for a in itertools.product(*box):
        if all(dd(a,x)<=r for x,r in cons): sols.append(a)
    return sols, len(inn)
OTHER=[a for n,a in CSSVAL.items()]

import json, itertools, random, sys
def all_points(step=4):
    return [(r,g,b) for r in range(0,256,step) for g in range(0,256,step) for b in range(0,256,step)]
if __name__=="__main__":
    step=int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv)>1 else 4
    part=int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv)>2 else 0
    pts=all_points(step)
    CH=25000
    chunk=pts[part*CH:(part+1)*CH]
    data=[]
    for h,ns in probe(["#%02X%02X%02X"%p for p in chunk]):
        if ns: data.append((h, strip(ns[0])))
    json.dump(data, open("/tmp/t/dense_%d_%d.json"%(step,part),"w"))
    print(len(data))

exec(open("/tmp/t/model.py").read())
data=load_dense(4)
items=list(CSSVAL.items())
def dd(a,x): return sum((a[i]-x[i])**2 for i in range(3))
orders=collections.Counter()
amb=0
for x,t in data:
    ds=sorted(((dd(a,x),n) for n,a in items))
    mn=ds[0][0]
    tl=[n for v,n in ds if v==mn]
    if len(tl)>1:
        if t in tl: 
            for o in tl:
                if o!=t: orders[(t,o)]+=1
        else: amb+=1
print("ambiguous",amb)
# check consistency with reverse alphabetical
def ra(a,b): return a>b
bad=[]
for (w,l),c in orders.items():
    if not ra(w,l): bad.append((w,l,c))
print("order constraints",len(orders))
print("inconsistent with reverse-alpha:",bad[:20], len(bad))
PY

    for a in range(120,140):
        for b in range(120,140):
            for v in range(120,139):
                p=[0,0,0]; p[axis]=v
                others=[k for k in range(3) if k!=axis]
                p[others[0]]=a; p[others[1]]=b
                p=tuple(p)
                q=list(p); q[axis]+=1; q=tuple(q)
                if d.get(p) and d.get(q):
                    if {d[p],d[q]}=={'grey','gray'}:
                        m=list(p); m[axis]+=0.5; pts.append(m)
print("flips",len(pts))
print(fit_plane(pts))
PY

def flips_between(A,B,rng=(100,200),step=2):

def solve_from_plane(aB, n, o, sign=1):

    return tuple(aB[i]+t*n[i] for i in range(3)), t

"mate":"Theme for blending i3 into MATE",
}
order=["slate","alphare","ubuntu","flat-gray","purple","archlinux","default","debian","oceanic-next","base16-tomorrow","okraits","icelines","solarized","deep-purple","tomorrow-night-80s","seti","lime","gruvbox","mate"]

slots = ["separator","background","statusline","focused_workspace","active_workspace","inactive_workspace","urgent_workspace",
         "client.focused","client.focused_inactive","client.unfocused","client.urgent"]
def emit(name):
    d=themes[name]
    lines=["---","meta:",'  description: "%s"'%descs[name],"colors:"]
    used=[]
    idx=0
    vals={}
    for s in slots:
        if s.startswith("client."):
            v=d.get(s)
            if v is None: continue
        else:
            v=d.get(s)
            if v is None: continue
            if isinstance(v,list): v=list(v)
            else: v=[v]
        vals[s]=v
    # colors map: assign names c1..cn to distinct values in order of slots
    def name_for(hexv):
        if hexv in name_for.m: return name_for.m[hexv]
        name_for.n+=1
        nm="c%d"%name_for.n
        name_for.m[hexv]=nm
        return nm
    name_for.m={}; name_for.n=0
    # first collect all values in slot order
    for s in slots:
        if s not in vals: continue
        for h in vals[s]:
            name_for(h)
    for h,nm in name_for.m.items():
        lines.append('  %s: "%s"'%(nm,h))
    lines.append("window_colors:")
    for s in ["client.focused","client.focused_inactive","client.unfocused","client.urgent"]:
        key=s.split(".")[1]
        if s not in vals: continue
        lines.append("  %s:"%key)
        lines.append("    border: %s"%name_for.m[vals[s][0]])
        lines.append("    background: %s"%name_for.m[vals[s][1]])
        lines.append("    text: %s"%name_for.m[vals[s][2]])
        lines.append("    indicator: %s"%name_for.m[vals[s][3]])
    lines.append("bar_colors:")
    for s in ["background","statusline","separator"]:
        if s in vals: lines.append("  %s: %s"%(s,name_for.m[vals[s][0]]))
    for s in ["focused_workspace","active_workspace","inactive_workspace","urgent_workspace"]:
        if s not in vals: continue
        lines.append("  %s:"%s)
        lines.append("    border: %s"%name_for.m[vals[s][0]])
        lines.append("    background: %s"%name_for.m[vals[s][1]])
        lines.append("    text: %s"%name_for.m[vals[s][2]])
    open("/tmp/ex/theme_%s.yaml"%name,"w").write("\n".join(lines)+"\n")
    return "\n".join(lines)
for t in order: emit(t)
print("\n".join(emit("flat-gray").split("\n")))
print("=== order:",order)

import subprocess, re, os, json
ENV=dict(os.environ); ENV["PATH"]="/tmp/bin:"+ENV["PATH"]
themes = """slate alphare ubuntu flat-gray purple archlinux default debian oceanic-next base16-tomorrow okraits icelines solarized deep-purple tomorrow-night-80s seti lime gruvbox mate""".split()
def ph(seq):
    # seq: list of 31 distinct-ish hexes
    cfg=["bar {","  colors {",
      "    separator "+seq[0],
      "    background "+seq[1],
      "    statusline "+seq[2],
      "    focused_workspace %s %s %s"%(seq[3],seq[4],seq[5]),
      "    active_workspace %s %s %s"%(seq[6],seq[7],seq[8]),
      "    inactive_workspace %s %s %s"%(seq[9],seq[10],seq[11]),
      "    urgent_workspace %s %s %s"%(seq[12],seq[13],seq[14]),
      "  }","}"]
    idx=15
    for c in ["focused","focused_inactive","unfocused","urgent"]:
        cfg.append("client.%s %s %s %s %s"%(c,seq[idx],seq[idx+1],seq[idx+2],seq[idx+3])); idx+=4
    return "\n".join(cfg)+"\n"
S1=["#%02X%02X%02X"%(i*3%256,(i*7)%256,(i*11)%256) for i in range(1,32)]
S2=["#%02X%02X%02X"%(255-(i*5)%256,(255-(i*13)%256),(255-(i*17)%256)) for i in range(1,32)]
open("t1.cfg","w").write(ph(S1)); open("t2.cfg","w").write(ph(S2))
slots=["separator","background","statusline","focused_workspace","active_workspace","inactive_workspace","urgent_workspace","client.focused","client.focused_inactive","client.unfocused","client.urgent"]
def parse(path):
    d={}
    for line in open(path).read().split("\n"):
        s=line.strip()
        if s.startswith(("separator ","background ","statusline ")):
            k,v=s.split(); d[k]=v
        else:
            m=re.match(r'^(\w+_workspace)\s+(#\S+)\s+(#\S+)\s+(#\S+)', s)
            if m: d[m.group(1)]=(m.group(2),m.group(3),m.group(4))
            elif s.startswith("client."):
                k,v=s.split(None,1); d[k]=tuple(v.split())
    return d
out={}
for t in themes:
    r1=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable",t,"-c","t1.cfg","-o","o1.cfg"],capture_output=True,env=ENV,cwd="/tmp/ex")
    r2=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable",t,"-c","t2.cfg","-o","o2.cfg"],capture_output=True,env=ENV,cwd="/tmp/ex")
    if r1.returncode!=0 or r2.returncode!=0:
        print("ERR",t,r1.returncode,r1.stderr.decode()[:120]); continue
    d1=parse("o1.cfg"); d2=parse("o2.cfg")
    res={}
    for s in slots:
        if s in d1 and s in d2 and d1[s]!=d2[s]: res[s]=d1[s]
        elif s in d1 and s not in d2: res[s]=d1[s]
    out[t]=res
json.dump(out, open("themes2.json","w"), indent=1)
for t in themes:
    print(t, sorted(out[t].keys()))

{"command": "cd /tmp/t && python3 - <<'PY'
pairs=[l.split() for l in open("/tmp/t/css.txt").read().split("\n") if l.strip()]
skip={"cyan","magenta","gray","lightgoldenrod","rebeccapurple"}
extra=[("grey","#808080"),("lightslategrey","#778899"),("aqua","#00FFFF"),("fuchsia","#FF00FF")]
seen=set(); rows=[]
for n,h in pairs:
    if n in skip: continue
    rows.append((n,h)); seen.add(n)
for n,h in extra:
    if n not in seen: rows.append((n,h)); seen.add(n)
# add extras found empirically
rows.append(("lightgoldenrodyellow","#FAFAD2"))
# order: reversed css order for tie-break, then extras
order=[n for n,_ in rows][::-1]
# put the extras first so they win ties (empirically lightslategray wins over lightslategrey)
extras_first=["lightgoldenrodyellow","lightslategray","gray"]
vals={'gray':(128.3334,128.3334,128.3334),'lightslategray':(119,135,154),'lightgoldenrodyellow':(250,250,210)}
out=[]
for n in extras_first:
    v=vals[n]; out.append((n, v[0],v[1],v[2]))
for n in order:
    if n in [e[0] for e in extras_first]: continue
    h=dict(rows)[n]
    r=int(h[1:3],16); g=int(h[3:5],16); b=int(h[5:7],16)
    out.append((n,r,g,b))
with open("/tmp/t/db.rs","w") as f:
    f.write("// Color name database (name, red, green, blue).\n")
    f.write("// Order matters: it is the tie-break order for equidistant colors.\n")
    f.write("pub static DB: &[(&str, f64, f64, f64)] = &[\n")
    for n,r,g,b in out:
        f.write('    ("%s", %s, %s, %s),\n'%(n, float(r), float(g), float(b)))
    f.write("];\n")
print(len(out), "entries")
print(open("/tmp/t/db.rs").read()[:400])
PY"}

cd /workspace && grep -cE "\(\"(aqua|fuchsia)\"" src/db.rs; python3 - <<'PY'
pairs=[l.split() for l in open("/tmp/t/css.txt").read().split("\n") if l.strip()]
skip={"cyan","magenta","gray","lightgoldenrod","rebeccapurple","aqua","fuchsia","lightgoldenrodyellow"}
rows=[(n,h) for n,h in pairs if n not in skip]
rows+=[("grey","#808080"),("lightslategrey","#778899")]
d=dict(rows)
extras_first=[("lightgoldenrodyellow",250.0,250.0,210.0),("lightslategray",119.0,135.0,154.0),("gray",128.3334,128.3334,128.3334)]
order=[n for n,_ in rows][::-1]
out=list(extras_first)
for n in order:
    if n in [e[0] for e in extras_first]: continue
    h=d[n]
    out.append((n,float(int(h[1:3],16)),float(int(h[3:5],16)),float(int(h[5:7],16))))
with open("/workspace/src/db.rs","w") as f:
    f.write("// Color name database used by `--to-theme`.\n")
    f.write("// Entries are (name, red, green, blue); the order is the tie-break order.\n")
    f.write("pub static DB: &[(&str, f64, f64, f64)] = &[\n")
    for n,r,g,b in out: f.write('    ("%s", %s, %s, %s),\n'%(n,r,g,b))
    f.write("];\n")
print(len(out))
PY
grep -E "aqua|fuchsia" src/db.rs

## What was built
A from-scratch Rust re-implementation of the `i3-style` tool (originally a clap-2 +
serde-yaml + colornamer based Rust program).  No third-party crates are used, so
`compile.sh` only needs `cargo build --release`.

```
Cargo.toml          crate manifest (no dependencies)
compile.sh          builds target/release/i3-style and copies it to ./executable
src/main.rs         entry point, flow, panic reproduction, `--to-theme` extraction
src/cli.rs          clap-2 compatible argument parser / help / error messages
src/theme.rs        theme model + YAML emitter (exact formatting)
src/config.rs       i3 config rewriting (bar blocks / colours / client.* lines)
src/colors.rs       colour parsing + nearest-colour lookup ("colornamer")
src/db.rs           colour name database (name, r, g, b) - order = tie-break order
src/yaml.rs         tiny YAML subset parser (theme files)
src/panics.rs       helpers that reproduce the original's panic messages
themes/*.yaml       the 19 built-in themes, extracted by observing the binary
```

## Behaviour that was reverse engineered (and is reproduced)
* CLI: help/version text, `--list-all` (order + column width 18), error messages
  ("error: Found argument ...", "error: The argument '--x <file>' requires a value ..."),
  error *usage* lines list only the options that are present (plus `--to-theme`,
  which always has a default value).
* theme lookup: known theme name first, otherwise treated as a file path
  (`Could not open theme: X - <io error>` + " Use `i3-style --list-all` ...").
* config location: `$HOME/.i3/config` then `$HOME/.config/i3/config`;
  missing => `Could not find i3 config` (exit 1).  `HOME` unset => panic
  `src/main.rs:47:46` (`Result::unwrap()` on `NotPresent`).
* config reading: `File::open` -> panic `src/writer.rs:24:40`,
  `read_to_string` -> panic `src/writer.rs:45:34`.
* no `-o`/`-s`  => themed config is written to **stdout**, no validation at all.
* `-o`/`-s`     => `/tmp/i3-style/<secs+millis>/` is created, `config-input` and
  `config-output` are written, `saving config at X to .../config-input` is printed
  on stderr, then `i3 -C -c <original path>` validates.
  Validation failure => `Could not validate config.\nUse \`i3 -C -c X\` ...`;
  i3 missing      => `Could not validate config with \`i3 -C -c X\` (is i3 in the PATH?) <io error>`.
* `-s` writes back to the input file, `-o` to the given file, `-r` then runs
  `i3-msg reload` (`Could not reload config with i3-msg: <io error>`).
* config rewriting rules (see tests in /tmp/tc/cfgs):
  * `bar` blocks are found by first token == `bar`; `colors {` inside them too.
  * inside `colors` blocks unknown directives are *dropped*, comments/blank lines kept.
  * workspace colour lines are rewritten as `{indent}{key} {b} {bg} {t}` plus a
    trailing ` {parts[3]}` when the original line had a 4th token; inserted lines
    always carry a trailing space.
  * inserted block when the bar block has no `colors`: fixed `  colors {` /
    4-space entries / `  }`.
  * missing entries inside an existing `colors` block are appended just before its
    closing brace with indent = 2 x (indent of that closing brace).
  * single value lines (`separator`, `background`, `statusline`) fall back to
    `parts[1]` of the original line when the theme does not define them, which
    panics (`src/writer.rs:252:44`, index out of bounds) when the line has no value.
  * `client.*` lines are rewritten in place (indent kept) and missing ones are
    appended at the end in the order focused, focused_inactive, unfocused, urgent.

  prints the YAML document.  Index panics reproduce `src/theme.rs:487:52`,
  `493:53`, `499:53`, `506:44`, `507:48`, `518:44`, `519:48`, `530:44`, `531:48`,
  `547:44`, `548:48`, `549:42`, `564:44`, `565:48`, `566:42`, `579:44`, `580:48`,
  `581:42`, `594:44`, `595:48`, `596:42` and happen in *config* order, while the
  generated `colors:` map is ordered canonically
  (separator, background, statusline, focused_workspace, inactive_workspace,
  urgent_workspace, focused, focused_inactive, unfocused, urgent).
  `active_workspace` colours are never collected.
* invalid hex colour tokens panic inside colornamer
  (`.../colornamer-0.1.0/src/color.rs:46:9` for a bad length, `:53:13` for a bad
  digit); the token is upper-cased in the message.

## Verification
* all 418 combinations (22 hand written configs x 19 themes) produce byte
  identical output/exit codes.
* `assets/minimal-config-solarized.expected` and
  `assets/minimal-config-testtheme.expected` are reproduced exactly (the latter
  is produced by the built-in theme `alphare`).
* 600 randomized configs: identical output for every theme application and for
  `--to-theme`, except 3 cases (0.5 %) - see limitations.

## Known limitations
1. **colour naming is only ~99.5 % accurate.**  The original uses the
   `colornamer` crate whose database is not fully recoverable from behaviour
   alone.  The reconstructed database is the CSS colour list (minus
   `cyan`, `magenta`, `gray`, `lightgoldenrod`, `rebeccapurple`, plus `aqua`,
   `fuchsia`, `grey`, `lightslategrey`) plus three entries found empirically:
   `gray` = (128.33,128.33,128.33), `lightslategray` = (119,135,154),
   `lightgoldenrodyellow` = (250,250,210) (`#FAFAD2`).
   The tie-break order is a reverse alphabetical CSS order, which was the best
   fit found.  Remaining known mismatches: a handful of colours where the
   original answers `grey` while this implementation answers `gray`
   (e.g. `#899F5A`, `#9B8763`, `#9B9359`) - the true `gray` database entry is
   probably not a pure grey, more probe data would be needed to pin it down.
2. The `ScanError { mark: Marker { index: .. } }` text for invalid theme YAML
   uses an approximated byte index (the line/column are exact).
3. Only a YAML subset is parsed for user supplied theme files (block mappings,
   flow mappings, quotes, comments); exotic YAML may fail where libyaml succeeds.
EOF
git add -A && git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=agent commit -q -m "Reimplement i3-style from behaviour observation" && git log --oneline | head -3 && git status --short | head"}

   - Exact line-rewriting rules for `bar {}`/`colors {}` blocks (indent-doubling for inserted entries, trailing spaces, dropped unknown directives, `parts[3]` carry-over, index-out-of-bounds panic sites)
   - `client.*` replacement in place + appended missing lines
   - `--to-theme` YAML emission, canonical color collection order vs. config-order panic sites, and the colornamer hex parsing/panic locations

3. **Verified**: 418/418 (22 configs × 19 themes) byte-identical outputs, both bundled `assets/*.expected` files reproduced exactly, 600 randomized configs identical except 3 (0.5 %) colour-naming cases.
